extracted.intended_audience: LaTeX/TikZ users writing diagrams (matrices, trees) — intermediate/advanced TeX users
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating and laying out TikZ/PGF matrix cell pictures and tree (child) structures, including spacing, anchoring, naming, growth, and edge rules. Covers options, styles, and special path operations used when producing diagrams with TikZ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Row-end command \\ optional spacing argument
rubrics_metrics.description: The row-end command \\ allows you to provide an optional argument, which must be a dimension. This dimension will be added to the list in row sep.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The value is added as extra row separation between the line being ended and the next line; you may use keywords between origins and between borders in this argument to locally overrule the standard setting for that line pair. Useful to locally tweak spacing between specific rows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cell separation (&) optional spacing list
rubrics_metrics.description: The cell separation character & also takes an optional argument, which must be a spacing list. This spacing list is added to the column sep.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This has similar effect to the \\ optional argument for rows. The optional spacing list can only be given the first time a new column is started (usually in the first row); subsequent usages in later rows have no effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=every cell
rubrics_metrics.description: style=every cell is a style installed at the beginning of each cell picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Setting this style to draw will not cause all nodes to be drawn since draw has to be passed to each node individually. Inside this style, the counters \pgfmatrixcurrentrow and \pgfmatrixcurrentcolumn are available to access current row/column.

rubrics_metrics.name: cells=(options) shorthand
rubrics_metrics.description: cells=(cid:104)options(cid:105) adds the given options to the style every cell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is shorthand for set style={{every cell}+=[options]}. Useful to apply the same options to every cell while keeping the matrix options concise.

rubrics_metrics.name: nodes=(options) shorthand
rubrics_metrics.description: nodes=(cid:104)options(cid:105) adds the given options to the style every node inside the matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a shorthand for set style={{every node}+=[options]}. Main use is to install options for nodes inside the matrix that should not apply to the matrix node itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-row/column/cell styles (column N, every odd/even column, row N, every odd/even row, row i column j)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can define styles that apply to entire columns, odd/even columns, entire rows, odd/even rows, or a specific cell via style=column <number>, style=every odd column, style=every even column, style=row <number>, style=every odd row, style=every even row, style=row <r> column <c>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than one of these styles is defined they are executed in a specified order (every cell style is executed before these). Use these to change alignment, color, or other per-row/column/cell appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: nodes={...} / nodes option on matrix
rubrics_metrics.description: The matrix option nodes={...} sets options that are applied to node elements inside the matrix (e.g., fill, minimum size).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to give a common appearance to all node cells (example nodes={fill=blue!20,minimum size=5mm}).

rubrics_metrics.name: execute at begin/end/empty cell
rubrics_metrics.description: execute at begin cell=(code), execute at end cell=(code), execute at empty cell=(code) execute the given code at the beginning/end of each nonempty cell or inside each empty cell respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to factor repeated code that every cell needs. The matrix library uses these for matrix-of-nodes: execute at begin cell=\node\bgroup and execute at end cell=\egroup; execute at empty cell can supply a placeholder like \node{--}.

rubrics_metrics.name: matrix anchor vs anchor option
rubrics_metrics.description: matrix anchor=(anchor) sets the anchor for the matrix itself only; anchor=(anchor) sets the anchor for the matrix and (by inheritance) the nodes inside unless overridden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use matrix anchor when you want to shift/anchor the matrix as a whole without changing the anchors of nodes inside. Example shows matrix anchor=west vs anchor=west behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: anchor=(node.anchor) to anchor matrix by an internal node
rubrics_metrics.description: anchor=(node).(anchor) form allows the matrix anchor argument to refer to an anchor of a node defined inside the matrix, causing the whole matrix to be shifted so that that node anchor lies at the matrix position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is useful to align the matrix based on an internal node's anchor (example: matrix anchor=inner node.south).

rubrics_metrics.name: ampersand replacement
rubrics_metrics.description: ampersand replacement=(macro name) prevents making & an active character and defines the given macro to be equal to \pgfmatrixnextcell inside matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when & cannot be made active (e.g., matrix used in macro arguments or containing tabular environments). Example: ampersand replacement=\& then use \& to separate columns.

rubrics_metrics.name: child operation placement and syntax rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The child operation (child[(options)]foreach variables in {values}{child path}) should directly follow a completed node operation or another child operation; TikZ scans and stores each child and its arguments until a non-child path operation is reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because children are collected before generating nodes, text inside child arguments is fixed (no verbatim). The optional foreach part allows creating multiple children from a list of values. The child path typically begins with a node specification; if missing, an empty coordinate child node is automatically added. The child path ends with an edge from parent operation which is added automatically if not given.

rubrics_metrics.name: first/last node semantics inside child path (child node and edge from parent)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first node in the child path is the child node; if no first node exists the child node defaults to a coordinate. The child path ends with an edge from parent operation (inserted automatically if omitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nodes following the edge from parent will be placed on the edge (as if pos was set). You can give options to edge from parent to style the connecting edge; nodes after edge can be labeled or positioned along the edge.

rubrics_metrics.name: automatic naming of child nodes
rubrics_metrics.description: If you do not assign a name to a child node, TikZ assigns names by counting: first child of parent becomes parent-1, second parent-2, etc., and this naming recurses (parent-2-1, ...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you assign a name manually, no automatic duplicate name is added; however counting continues, so later auto-generated names reflect position regardless of manual names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options placement rules for trees and children
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules: (1) Options for the whole tree are given before the root node. (2) Options for the root node are given directly to the root node operation. (3) Options for all children can be given between the root node and the first child. (4) Options applying to a specific child path are given to the child operation. (5) Options applying to the node of a child (but not the whole child path) are given to the node command inside the child path.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These rules determine scope: root-node-local options do not affect children; options between root and first child apply to all children; use styles every child, every child node, or level <n> for more systematic settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=every child, style=every child node, style=level N
rubrics_metrics.description: style=every child is used at the beginning of each child (as if options were given to child operation). style=every child node is used at the beginning of each child node in addition to every node. style=level <number> is used at the beginning of each set of children for that level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use level styles to change sibling distance, set styles progressively down the tree, and to apply level-specific formatting (examples using sibling distance and set style to modify every node).

rubrics_metrics.name: level distance option
rubrics_metrics.description: level distance=(distance) changes the distance between different levels of the tree, i.e., between the parent and the line on which its children are arranged. When given to a single child, this sets the distance for that child only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be set via per-child option or via level styles (level 1, level 2...). Use to control vertical (or radial) spacing between parent and children.

rubrics_metrics.name: sibling distance option
rubrics_metrics.description: sibling distance=(distance) specifies the distance between the anchors (centers) of the children of a parent node.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be configured per level via tikzstyle level N to control how tightly siblings are packed. Note: default growth function spaces children uniformly based on sibling distance.

rubrics_metrics.name: grow and grow' options
rubrics_metrics.description: grow=(direction) defines the direction the tree will grow (angles or text directions like down, up, left, right, north east, etc.) and installs the default growth function. grow' reverses child ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a side effect grow sets the sibling distance for the current level to 0pt: when given before the child list starts this causes children to lie on a line orthogonal to grow direction; when given locally to a child it places that child exactly at level distance in the given direction. Use intentionally to align children; beware of the zero sibling distance side-effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: growth parent anchor option
rubrics_metrics.description: growth parent anchor=(anchor) specifies which anchor of the parent node is used when computing children positions (default is center).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Child node's anchor is placed at the given parent anchor offset by level distance. Use growth parent anchor to align children relative to specific parent anchors (examples show aligning top/bottom).

rubrics_metrics.name: growth function option
rubrics_metrics.description: growth function=(macro name) lets you set a custom growth function; the macro will be called for each child and must transform the coordinate system so that the origin becomes where the current child should be anchored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When called \tikznumberofchildren is set to total number of children and \tikznumberofcurrentchild to the current child index. The macro may also rotate/scale the coordinate system. This is a low-level option for custom layouts (e.g., circle layouts); additional growth functions provided in the library.

rubrics_metrics.name: edge from parent operation and edge from parent path
rubrics_metrics.description: edge from parent is a path operation used inside child paths to insert the current edge-from-parent path; edge from parent path=(path) sets that path (default is (\tikzparentnode) -- (\tikzchildnode)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options given before edge from parent are applied to the whole child path and the style edge from parent is installed right before inserting the edge path (by default draws the edge). You can customize anchors via child anchor and parent anchor, change the edge into curves, dashed lines, etc. Nodes after edge from parent are placed on the edge (as if pos was used). Note that options inserted before the edge apply to the entire child, so you cannot have the child interior styled differently from the edge by using those options; instead style the child node separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: child anchor and parent anchor for edges
rubrics_metrics.description: child anchor=(anchor) and parent anchor=(anchor) specify which anchors of child/parent the edge from parent meets by setting \tikzchildanchor and \tikzparentanchor; specifying border sets anchor macros to empty string so the edge meets the border at an automatically calculated position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to control precise attachment points of edges on node shapes (e.g., child anchor=north to have edge meet the child at its north anchor).

rubrics_metrics.name: style=edge from parent
rubrics_metrics.description: style=edge from parent is inserted right before the edge from parent path and before the per-edge options are applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By default it draws the edge from parent; redefine it to change the default appearance of all parent-to-child edges (examples use red, thick drawing).
